subject: Urgent: authentication spike — request for IR plan, logs, and tabletop artifacts
messages:
From: security@acme-corp.com
To: jordan.blake@redwood.com
Cc: ops-lead@fintriage.com
Date: 2028-03-18T07:12:34-07:00
Subject: Unusual auth spike — immediate visibility requested

Jordan —

We just observed a sustained authentication spike from ~03:05–03:40 PT against several API keys associated with our Redwood integration (tenant acme-prod). The requests look like high-rate token refreshes; no obvious data exfil indicators in the cursory logs we held, but latency and error rates spiked downstream.

We need:
- Confirmation this was handled or isolated on your side
- A copy of your incident response plan excerpt covering API credential misuse (SIG / SOC2-relevant controls)
- Short sample logs (redacted) covering the time window 03:00–04:00 PT so our SecOps can cross-check

I'm attaching a short summary and a single-line log extract. Can you triage and tell us whether we should rotate any keys or take other immediate steps?

Thanks,
Claire Mendoza
Security Operations Lead
Acme Corp
attachments: acme_auth-spike-summary.pdf (pdf)

---

Date: 2028-03-18T07:27:50-07:00

Claire — thanks for the heads up and the summary. We’re picking this up as an incident and will route through our IR workflow. Immediate notes:

- I’ve opened SUP-9172 (link below) to track triage and customer communications.
- Short answer: no confirmed data exfil yet; we’re validating telemetry and quota/burst anomalies.
- Temporary recommended action: we advise rotating the API keys for any long-lived keys you suspect. I’ll coordinate a minimal-impact window if you prefer us to perform a rotation.

Next steps from our side (first 60 minutes):
1) Full trace & auth logs pull for 02:50–04:10 PT (will share redacted excerpts)
2) Snapshot of active sessions and token issuance for tenant acme-prod
3) Confirm whether any rate-limiting or WAF rules triggered
4) Deliver an IRP excerpt that maps to SIG/SOC2 control family CC4 (incident detection/response) — short, customer-friendly snippet

Marissa — I’m looped for the IRP excerpt and artifacts; can you prioritize the plan snippet and quick log pull? Karthik, can you start the logs trace and share any obvious anomalies?

I’ll follow up with a short status update in 30 minutes.

—Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
phone: +1 (415) 555-0182

From: marissa.cole@redwood.com
To: jordan.blake@redwood.com, security@acme-corp.com
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2028-03-18T08:01:13-07:00
Subject: Re: Unusual auth spike — immediate visibility requested

Claire / Jordan — quick status and attached artifacts for initial triage.

What we did (first 45 mins):
- Pulled auth logs for tenant acme-prod (02:45–04:15 PT) and redacted PII. Sample attached: log-sample-20280318-07-zip.txt (see tab-delimited excerpt).
- Queried token issuance and active sessions; no large token dumps or suspicious export endpoints called.
- Confirmed no degraded disk or network activity that would indicate exfil pipe during window.
- Checked our rate-limiter & WAF triggers — one rule fired for a burst pattern; the requests were not escalating to other backend systems.

IRP excerpt (attached as PDF): contains the following high-level steps mapped to SOC2/SIG:
- Detection & initial classification: triage ownership assigned; severity: medium
- Containment: throttling policy applied; temporary rule to block the high-rate source for 15 mins
- Eradication: credential rotation guidance + steps for customer to rotate keys and revoke tokens
- Recovery: monitor bounded window for 24 hours; sanity checks on usage patterns
- Post-incident: tabletop & artifact handoff within 72 hours; full postmortem when available

Attachments: redwood_irp_excerpt.pdf, log-sample-20280318-07-zip.txt

Immediate ask for Acme: please confirm whether you want Redwood to perform key rotation (can schedule a 10-min maintenance window) or if you will rotate on your side. Also let us know a primary contact for the 1:1 post-incident tabletop (30–60 mins).

Karthik — share any brief observations you see in the logs here.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, jordan.blake@redwood.com
Cc: security@acme-corp.com
Date: 2028-03-18T12:46:02-07:00
Subject: Re: Unusual auth spike — immediate visibility requested

Quick technical notes (log excerpt summarized):
- Pattern: ~1200 auth attempts/minute from a narrow IP subnet for ~34 minutes; user-agent strings varied but signatures are similar to bot-driven refresh loops.
- No suspicious POST payloads to customer data endpoints in the sampled logs (all 200/401/429 responses).
- A handful (~6) of short-lived tokens were issued by our token service to clients in that window — we flagged those token IDs and recommend rotation for any long-lived keys tied to them.

Artifacts attached: log-sample-20280318-07-zip.txt (redacted), small index file with token IDs. I’ve pulled the token IDs and marked them in SUP-9172.

Recommendation: rotate keys for tenant acme-prod now and run the short 10-min revocation on our endpoint (we can do this together to reduce potential downtime). Post-rotation, we should run a 24-hour elevated monitoring window and schedule a 45-minute tabletop to review the response and produce a short postmortem.

—Karthik Iyer
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
attachments: log-sample-20280318-07-zip.txt

Claire — ping here when you’re ready and we’ll coordinate key rotation window.
